note: Proposed NEW JFR events derived from gap analysis of -Xlog log sites that no existing JFR event covers. These events DO NOT exist in the JDK 25 oracle (jfr metadata, 194 events); they are candidates for upstream proposal. Scope of this analysis: -Xlog:trimnative*,gc*,gc+region*,gc+ergo*,gc+humongous*,stringdedup*=info (127 uncovered firing sites). Each 'replaces' entry cites the HotSpot source file + verbatim log format string the event would make recoverable via JFR. Field types follow the oracle convention (long for time/bytes/counters, int for ids, float/double for ratios, boolean/String). startTime/duration follow the standard JFR event contract. Status note (2026-08-17): JDK 26 adds jdk.StringDeduplication (partial overlap — see rationale on StringDeduplicationStatistics). JDK 27 adds jdk.ShenandoahPromotionInformation (in metadata.xml, not yet released). JDK-8365306 (In Progress) will add a native-heap-trim JFR event. None of the other 9 proposed events have upstream work in progress. Critique pass 2 applied 2026-08-17 based on source analysis + GC engineer research: G1ConcurrentRefinement split into Sweep+Policy events, PSAdaptiveSizePolicy fields corrected (averaged vs last, naming), GCOverheadLimitExceeded extended with diagnostic fields, ZDirectorRule refined (early-exit semantics noted, missing rule-specific fields added), ShenandoahMMU priority elevated, ShenandoahReclaimProgress redesigned as single typed event, ShenandoahCardStatistics gated to cumulative-only, ZNMethodRegistration corrected (tableRebuilt field added).

proposed.label: String Deduplication Statistics
proposed.rationale: JDK 26 added jdk.StringDeduplication (JDK-8037914) with coarse counters (inspectedCount, deduplicatedCount, lastDeduplicated, totalDeduplicated). The remaining gap is byte-level data and the newUnknown metric. Consider proposing as an EXTENSION to jdk.StringDeduplication rather than a separate event: add dedupedBytes, totalDedupedBytes, newUnknown, newUnknownBytes, dedupedRatio to the existing event. The count fields (inspected, deduped) are already in JDK 26's event and need not be duplicated.

fields.name: newUnknown
fields.label: New Unknown (strings seen but not in dedup table)

replaces.logLine: Concurrent String Deduplication %zu (inspected), %zu/ (new unknown), %zu/ (deduped), total avg deduped/new unknown bytes ,  (total deduped), (total new unknown),  of

proposed.label: Shenandoah Card Statistics
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational (only) remembered-set card scanning emits cumulative dirty/clean card statistics per GC cycle with no JFR event. Per-worker stats are gated behind ShenandoahEnableCardStats and non-product builds; this event emits only the cumulative aggregate (workerId=-1 row). For JFR event design the per-worker rows should be either omitted or in a separate debug-level event. 'dirtyScannedObjects' is the count of heap objects visited as a result of dirty card scans — distinct from dirtyCards (card-table slot count). The maxConsecutiveDirty/Clean fields reflect card-table clustering patterns that affect scan efficiency.

replaces.logLine: Card stats: dirty %zu (max run: %zu), clean %zu (max run: %zu), dirty scans/objs %zu
Cumulative stats

proposed.label: Shenandoah Minimum Mutator Utilization
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah's MMU tracker prints GC utilization (GCU) and mutator utilization (MU) per completed phase with no JFR analogue. Not redundant with jdk.GCCPUTime: GCCPUTime gives raw user/sys/real CPU slices; this gives normalized MU% over the phase window. Low muPercent directly indicates mutator starvation — a production-critical signal. Phase values from source: 'Concurrent Young GC', 'Concurrent Global GC', 'Concurrent Bootstrap GC', 'OLD marking increment', 'last OLD marking increment', 'Mixed Concurrent GC'. The field 'periodSeconds' is the wall-clock window over which GCU/MU were measured — not a JFR @Timespan duration but a floating-point seconds scalar matching the log output.

fields.name: phase
fields.label: Phase (free-form string; values may change across JDK releases)

replaces.logLine: At end of %s: GCU: %.1f%%, MU: %.1f%% during period of %.3fs
At end of %s: GCU: %.1f%%, MU: %.1f%% for duration %.3fs (totals to be subsumed in next gc report)

proposed.label: Shenandoah Reclaim Progress
proposed.rationale: shenandoahMetrics.cpp's is_good_progress() evaluates four independent dimensions after each cycle: free-space vs ShenandoahCriticalFreeThreshold, used-space freed vs one region_size_bytes, and internal/external fragmentation delta vs 1% threshold. The function exits early on the first passing condition — so not all log lines always fire. This event captures all four dimensions in a single flat event (one per cycle) to avoid stream-join complexity. Units: freeActual/freeNeeded are bytes (long); usedFreed/usedNeededToFree are bytes; fragmentation fields are decimal fractions (0.01 = 1%). goodProgress=false in any dimension signals risk of degenerated GC fallback in subsequent cycles.

fields.name: usedNeededToFree
fields.label: Minimum Space to Free (bytes, = one region)

replaces.logLine: %s progress for free space: , need
%s progress for used space: , need
%s progress for internal fragmentation: %.1f%%, need %.1f%%
%s progress for external fragmentation: %.1f%%, need %.1f%%

proposed.label: ZGC NMethod Registration
proposed.rationale: ZGC requires all nmethods to have load barriers patched (registered). The NMethod table tracks live registrations and cumulative unregistrations. High unregistered counts can indicate classloader churn or code cache pressure — both correlate with ZGC barrier-patching overhead that shows as latency spikes. Emitted once per GC cycle as part of ZStat. Field semantics from ZNMethodTable.cpp: 'registeredNMethods' = current live count (_nregistered); 'unregisteredNMethods' = cumulative count since table creation (_nunregistered, NOT current). 'tableRebuilt' distinguishes a full table-rebuild (which resets _nunregistered to zero) from organic unregistration — necessary to avoid misinterpreting a zero-crossing as a flush.

fields.name: unregisteredNMethods
fields.label: Cumulative Unregistered NMethods (resets on table rebuild)

fields.name: tableRebuilt
fields.label: NMethod Table Was Rebuilt This Cycle

replaces.logLine: NMethods: %zu registered, %zu unregistered

proposed.label: GC Overhead Limit Exceeded
proposed.rationale: Fires immediately before the JVM throws OutOfMemoryError: GC Overhead Limit exceeded. Implemented in G1 and Parallel GC only (not Serial/ZGC/Shenandoah). The condition is: GC time ≥ GCTimeLimit% (default 98) AND free space < GCHeapFreeLimit% (default 2) for GCOverheadLimitThreshold consecutive GCs (default 5). The three diagnostic fields (gcTimePercent, freeSpacePercent, consecutiveViolations) make the event self-contained — without them a consumer cannot tell whether the OOM was time-driven or space-driven. gcId is the last-completed GC id (GCId::peek()), not an active GC. Collector field distinguishes G1 from Parallel since the threshold computation differs slightly.

replaces.logLine: GC Overhead Limit exceeded too often (%zu).
GC Overhead Limit: GC Time %f Free Space %f Counter %zu
GC Overhead Limit exceeded too often (%zu).

proposed.label: Native Heap Trim
proposed.rationale: The JVM periodically calls malloc_trim/madvise to return RSS to the OS after GC. The log line (trimNativeHeap.cpp) records before/after RSS and delta, but no JFR event carries this. Especially valuable on containerised deployments where RSS spikes are monitored closely. detailsAvailable=false when /proc/self/status is unavailable (non-Linux or restricted containers). JDK-8365306 (In Progress) confirms upstream interest: its design explicitly requests an event-driven trim event with 'when, how much RSS recovered, and duration'. Our field schema matches that description exactly — align with whatever schema JDK-8365306 adopts rather than proposing a competing one.

fields.name: deltaBytes
fields.label: RSS Freed (bytes, beforeBytes - afterBytes; negative = RSS grew)

fields.name: detailsAvailable
fields.label: RSS Details Available (false on non-Linux or restricted containers)

proposed.label: G1 Concurrent Refinement Sweep
proposed.rationale: G1 concurrent refinement sweeps the dirty-card queue (DCQS) between pauses. This event fires once per sweep cycle — potentially multiple times per GC pause. It captures the operational outcome: how many cards were scanned, which were clean/dirty/cset, and timing sub-totals. Counterpart: jdk.G1ConcurrentRefinementPolicy fires once per young-GC pause with the policy's predictive state. Field notes: cardsNoCrossRegion are within-region references filtered early (high value = good heap locality). cardsRefersToCset/cardsStillRefersToCset: the latter are cards that still point into the CSet after refinement (CSet churn indicator). cardsPendingFromGC is the portion of the queue seeded by GC operations rather than mutator writes (key for diagnosing GC-driven refinement pressure).

fields.name: cardsNoCrossRegion
fields.label: Cards With No Cross-Region Reference (filtered early)

fields.name: cardsRefersToCset
fields.label: Cards Referring to Collection Set at Scan Time

fields.name: cardsStillRefersToCset
fields.label: Cards Still Referring to CSet After Refinement

fields.name: cardsPending
fields.label: Cards Pending in Queue After Sweep

fields.name: cardsPendingFromGC
fields.label: Cards Pending Due to GC Activity (subset of cardsPending)

replaces.logLine: Concurrent refinement: wanted %u, pending cards: %zu (pending-from-gc %zu), card stats: scanned %zu, clean %zu, not-clean %zu, not-parsable %zu, refers-to-cset %zu, still-refers-to-cset %zu (pre-sweep %.2fms card-refine %.2fms)

proposed.label: G1 Concurrent Refinement Policy Update
proposed.rationale: Fires once per young-GC pause when G1Policy::record_young_collection_end() adjusts the pending-cards target and refinement thread count. This is the policy/analytics counterpart to jdk.G1ConcurrentRefinementSweep (which fires per-sweep). The predicted vs actual refinement rates and the pending-cards target are the primary levers for diagnosing whether G1's adaptive refinement is keeping up with write-barrier pressure. exceededGoal=true means the inter-pause sweep period overran the goal window, which typically leads to G1 increasing threadsWanted.

fields.name: pendingCardsFromGC
fields.label: Cards Pending Due to GC Activity

replaces.logLine: Concurrent refinement: wanted %u, pending cards target %zu, predicted refine rate %.2f, dirtied card rate %.2f, goal %.2fms%s

proposed.label: ZGC Director Rule Evaluation
proposed.rationale: ZGC's director evaluates rules to decide whether to trigger GC. The gc+director log tag records each rule evaluation with context data. IMPORTANT design note: make_minor_gc_decision and make_major_gc_decision both return on the first triggered rule (early-exit). This means in practice at most one Minor rule and one Major rule fires per cycle, and only the winning rule produces a log line. The event as designed fires for the winning rule only — 'triggered' is therefore always true for emitted events. If observability of skipped rules is desired, the director must be refactored to evaluate all rules unconditionally before returning (a functional change). Rule-specific fields are sparse: Timer only uses timeUntilGC; High Usage only uses freeBytes; Warmup uses usedBytes+usedThreshold; AllocationRate uses maxAllocRate+freeBytes+timeUntilGC+timeUntilOOM+gcDuration+allocRateVariancePct; Major AllocationRate uses extraYoungGCTime+oldGCTime+lookahead. The sparse-field design may receive upstream pushback — per-rule-type events may be preferred. Generation values 'Young'/'Old' align with JFR convention (ZYoungGarbageCollection / ZOldGarbageCollection), not the log's 'Minor'/'Major' display strings.

proposed.label: Parallel GC Adaptive Size Policy
proposed.rationale: Parallel GC's AdaptiveSizePolicy runs a feedback loop after each GC to resize eden and survivor toward throughput and pause-time goals. The gc+ergo log tag emits the full policy state but no JFR event captures this. Understanding why generation sizes oscillate or GC overhead increases currently requires log parsing. Field notes: *Estimate fields are the smoothed/padded averages actually used for sizing decisions; *Last fields are raw samples from the most recent GC — both are logged and both are needed to diagnose whether averages are being pulled by spikes. 'mutatorIntervalSec' = time between GC end and next GC start (the 'gc-distance' in logs). 'survivorOverflow' = survivor space too small, some objects promoted to old that wouldn't normally be — softer than PromotionFailed. 'desiredEdenDelta' = requested change (may be clipped by resize_inner). 'minFreeBytes' = computed from promoted average and 10-minute promotion rate lookahead — needed to interpret shrinkBytes.

fields.label: Mutator Interval Average (s, time between GC end and next GC start)

fields.name: promotedBytesEstimate
fields.label: Promoted Bytes Estimate (padded average used for sizing)

fields.label: Promotion Rate Last GC (MB/s, raw sample)

fields.name: survivorOverflow
fields.label: Survivor Space Overflowed (objects promoted that shouldn't be)

fields.name: desiredEdenDelta
fields.label: Requested Eden Size Change (bytes, negative = shrink)

fields.name: minFreeBytes
fields.label: Old Gen Minimum Free Threshold (bytes, from promotion lookahead)

proposed.label: Shenandoah Collection Decision
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational mode's regulator/control FSM decides each cycle: collect young, old, global, mixed, or interrupt/resume/cancel an in-progress cycle. This decision is scattered across shenandoahRegulatorThread.cpp and shenandoahOldHeuristics.cpp with no JFR event. IMPORTANT: the 'decision' field values must align with the actual GCMode enum or the regulator log lines — the source uses 'servicing_old', 'none', and the request types ('young collection accepted', 'old collection accepted', etc.), NOT free-form short names. Pending clarification: the exact strings should be derived from GCMode enum values in shenandoahGenerationalControlThread.hpp. The mixed-collection fields (mixedCandidates, mixedRegionsSelected, oldEvacuationBudget, defragRegions) are only meaningful when a mixed GC is selected; they are zero for other decision types. 'immediateGarbagePercent' comes from shenandoahAdaptiveHeuristics — the immediate-garbage ratio compared against ShenandoahImmediateThreshold (default 0.65); when this exceeds the threshold an immediate-garbage collection is triggered.
